source.title: A developmentally restricted γδ T cell-IL-17A axis supports mouse heart regeneration

search_terms: gamma delta T cell heart regeneration

reported_study.model: neonatal versus older mouse cardiac injury
reported_study.observation: Neonatal injured hearts accumulate a γδ T-cell population not seen in older nonregenerative injured hearts.
reported_study.reported_results: Reduced heart regeneration, altered immune infiltration, impaired cardiac function with perturbations.
reported_study.mechanistic_interpretation: γδ T cell-derived IL-17A acts on myeloid cells to promote rapid self-limited inflammation and clearance of apoptotic cells.
reported_study.caveat: Apoptotic cell clearance here is not demonstrated to be clearance of profibrotic fibroblast lineage.
quantitative_unknowns: independent animal n by age and treatment

relation_to_prior.biological_specificity: Context-specific neonatal γδ IL-17A cannot be extrapolated to adult chronic inflammation, fibrosis, or human therapy.

next_TOPA: Obtain full article, figure legends, supplemental methods, source data and deposited accession IDs, if any.
Extract neonatal and older control groups, independent animal n, knockout and IL-17 perturbation details, timing and functional effects.
Check if IL-17A axis causes apoptotic debris clearance only or also fate-resolved loss of activated cardiac fibroblasts; do not equate the two.
Reconstruct self-limited immune-response time course and compare against chronic-inflammation controls.
Keep immune timing root independent of existing ADAM17 mechanical and spinal Gata4/EV roots.
